post_title: On Black Friday (November 27, 2026), what will be the deepest percentage-off discount advertised on the childrensplace.com homepage?

question.title: On Black Friday (November 27, 2026), what will be the deepest percentage-off discount advertised on the childrensplace.com homepage?
question.description:
The Children's Place, Inc. (PLCE), the Secaucus, New Jersey-based children's apparel retailer with roughly 514 North American stores plus the Gymboree brand, filed for Chapter 11 protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey on November 8, 2026, seeking a court-supervised sale of substantially all its assets (bids due December 9, 2026; sale targeted for completion by the end of December 2026). Store-closing sales had already begun on November 6, 2026, and on November 12, 2026 a joint venture of GA Group, Tiger Group, SB360 Capital Partners, Gordon Brothers and Hilco Global announced court-approved going-out-of-business sales at all The Children's Place and Gymboree locations in the United States and Canada, together with an online inventory liquidation on both e-commerce platforms. Under the liquidators' consulting agreement, the sale term runs to a February 28, 2027 termination date.

Pricing so far: the launch event was a "Total Inventory Blowout" advertised as 25–60% off everything, in stores and online, and news coverage through mid-November described a childrensplace.com banner reading "Everything Must Go / All Stores Closing" with 30–60% off. As of November 13, 2026 the homepage (https://www.childrensplace.com/us/home) displays promotional messaging such as "30–60% off everything", "40–60% off", "all clearance 60% off+", "all outerwear 30% off" and "extra 20% off everything with code WOW20", while individual product cards carry badges in the 30–45%-off range. The site's promos rotate quickly (an on-site clearance countdown was due to expire in mid-November), and liquidators running going-out-of-business sales normally ratchet markdowns deeper as inventory clears, with the deepest levels typically appearing in the final weeks before the termination date. Black Friday, November 27, 2026, is the biggest promotional day in U.S. retail, so how deep the markdown goes that day is genuinely uncertain.

Sources: company announcement page https://corporate.childrensplace.com/what-we-announced ; joint venture release https://gagroup.com/blog/going-out-of-business-sales-underway-at-all-the-childrens-place-and-gymboree-locations .

Resolution data note: childrensplace.com's root domain only redirects and is blocked to automated archiving, but the storefront homepage at /us/home is captured by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine roughly once or twice a day (typically around 08:50 and 20:50 UTC), and those archived pages render the full promotional banner text, so the November 27, 2026 capture can be read directly at https://web.archive.org/web/20261127170000/https://www.childrensplace.com/us/home .

question.resolution_criteria: Resolution uses the capture of The Children's Place homepage at https://www.childrensplace.com/us/home held by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine whose timestamp is closest to 17:00 UTC (12:00 US Eastern) on November 27, 2026 — the capture served at https://web.archive.org/web/20261127170000/https://www.childrensplace.com/us/home — and where two captures are equally close, the earlier one is used. The resolution value is the single largest percentage figure presented in the promotional text of that captured homepage (its banners, headlines, category tiles and deal modules) as a reduction off merchandise prices, including "up to" and range wording, with a range or "X% off+" read as its highest figure (e.g. "take 30–60% off everything" → 60; "all clearance 60% off+" → 60; "up to 70% off select styles" → 70). Percentage figures shown on individual product cards as a sale-price-versus-original-price comparison, and percentages relating to shipping, rewards, financing or fabric composition, do not count. Stated discounts are never combined or stacked with one another. If the captured homepage renders normally but displays no qualifying discount percentage, the value is 0.
question.fine_print: If the selected capture is an error page or renders no promotional content at all (for example a bot-block page or a script-only shell), the capture on November 27, 2026 that does render the homepage's promotional text and is closest to 17:00 UTC is used instead, taking the earlier one if two are equally close; if no capture dated November 27, 2026 renders the homepage, the closest such capture in time to 17:00 UTC on that date is used. Percentages present only inside banner images whose text cannot be read on the captured page do not count unless the same figure also appears as text. The value is the percentage number itself (a "70% off" promotion resolves as 70, not 0.70).
